description: OpenMRS HIV/ART-program vocabulary (CD4 monitoring, ARV/OI treatment plans, WHO clinical staging, adherence, and visit cadence) over SQL-on-FHIR Data Pipes projections of a real OpenMRS RefApp instance.

freshness.updateBehavior: An operator-triggered FULL FHIR_SEARCH run against the OpenMRS FHIR2 R4 endpoint recreates the sink projections; only succeeded runs with a source watermark are current.

views.name: analytics.hiv_observation_fact_v1
views.grain: Exactly one row per FHIR Observation, joined to its Patient by resource key. Effective dates outside 2020-01-01..2027-01-01 are excluded (a small number of source records carry clearly invalid dates, e.g. year 1919 or 5025).

columns.name: observation_id
columns.description: FHIR Observation resource identifier and stable row identity.

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier referenced by the observation.

columns.name: encounter_id
columns.description: FHIR Encounter resource identifier the observation was recorded within.

columns.name: patient_gender
columns.description: FHIR Patient.gender.

columns.name: patient_birth_date
columns.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate. Compute age at observation as (observed_at - patient_birth_date) rather than assuming a stored age column.

columns.name: obs_status
columns.description: FHIR Observation.status.

columns.name: observed_at
columns.description: FHIR Observation effective dateTime.

columns.name: concept_system
columns.description: Coding-system URI for concept_code; https://cielterminology.org when populated, otherwise null. Informational only — do not filter on this column; see concept_code's description for why.

columns.name: concept_code
columns.description: CIEL numeric concept code when the source Observation carries a CIEL-system coding (e.g. 5497 for CD4 count). NOT reliable as a filter: roughly half of this dataset's Observations for a given concept_name have no CIEL coding at all (concept_code and concept_system are then null) even though concept_name is populated identically either way. Filtering on concept_code silently undercounts — always filter on concept_name instead. Informational/cross-reference column only.

columns.name: concept_name
columns.description: Human-readable concept display name. A question naming a marker must constrain this field (or concept_code) rather than assume the view contains only that marker.

columns.name: value_numeric
columns.description: Populated only for numeric-valued concepts (e.g. CD4 count, CD4 percent, CD8 count). Null for coded or free-text observations; do not aggregate across unlike concepts or units.

columns.name: value_unit
columns.description: Unit for value_numeric, when the source Observation carries one.

columns.name: value_coded_code
columns.description: CIEL numeric code for a coded answer (e.g. Yes/No/Unknown for antiretroviral use, a WHO stage value, an adherence category). Populated only for coded-valued concepts.

columns.name: value_coded_name
columns.description: Human-readable label for value_coded_code.

columns.name: value_text
columns.description: Free-text value, populated only for the small number of concepts recorded as plain text rather than numeric or coded.

values.canonical: Overall drug adherence in last month
aliases: overall adherence in the past month
ARV adherence in the past week

terminology: Always filter and group by concept_name, never by concept_code. Verified against the live source: roughly half of this dataset's Observations for a well-populated concept (e.g. CD4 count, Antiretroviral plan, Current WHO HIV stage) have no CIEL-system coding at all, only OpenMRS's internal coding; concept_code and concept_system are null on exactly those rows, while concept_name is populated the same way regardless. Filtering on concept_code returns roughly half the true matching rows with no error or warning.

Concept codes, where present, are CIEL numeric codes (system https://cielterminology.org). HIV viral load (concept 856, concept_name 'HIV viral load') has only 3 recorded results in this demo instance; it is present in the vocabulary but is not a viable basis for a viral-suppression or treatment-failure demo question. CD4 count (5497) and CD4% (730) are the well-populated quantitative HIV markers.

HIV status itself is not recorded as a FHIR Condition in this dataset; a question about 'patients with HIV' or 'on treatment' must be answered from Antiretroviral plan/use or WHO stage observations (concept_name 'Antiretroviral plan', 'Antiretroviral use', or 'Current WHO HIV stage'), not from a condition table.

Recorded antiretroviral regimens (Primary regimen, concept 1155) skew toward older, Stavudine (d4T)-based combinations, consistent with a legacy ART-program data model; do not assume modern first-line regimens are represented.
A row has at most one of value_numeric, value_coded_code, or value_text populated, depending on concept_code; always branch on which one is non-null rather than assuming a fixed shape.

freshness.updateBehavior: Operator-triggered FULL FHIR_SEARCH against the OpenMRS FHIR2 R4 endpoint; query provenance carries run ID, source watermark, completion state, and observed lag.

examples.question: Show CD4 count results since 2026-01-01 with patient, value, and observed date.
examples.sql: SELECT patient_id, value_numeric, value_unit, observed_at FROM analytics.hiv_observation_fact_v1 WHERE concept_name = :concept_name AND observed_at >= :start_at ORDER BY observed_at

examples.question: Show the most recent WHO HIV stage recorded for each patient.
examples.sql: SELECT DISTINCT ON (patient_id) patient_id, value_coded_name, observed_at FROM analytics.hiv_observation_fact_v1 WHERE concept_name = :concept_name ORDER BY patient_id, observed_at DESC

views.name: analytics.hiv_visit_fact_v1
views.grain: Exactly one row per FHIR Encounter, joined to its Patient by resource key, with the immediately preceding visit for the same patient exposed directly. Visit start/end dates outside 2020-01-01..2027-01-01 are excluded (matching the observation fact's outlier-date exclusion).

columns.name: encounter_id
columns.description: FHIR Encounter resource identifier and stable row identity.

columns.name: patient_id
columns.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier referenced by the encounter.

columns.name: patient_gender
columns.description: FHIR Patient.gender.

columns.name: patient_birth_date
columns.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate.

columns.name: encounter_status
columns.description: FHIR Encounter.status.

columns.name: encounter_type
columns.description: FHIR Encounter type display name; almost all encounters in this demo instance are 'OPD Visit'.

columns.name: started_at
columns.description: FHIR Encounter.period.start.

columns.name: ended_at
columns.description: FHIR Encounter.period.end.

columns.name: prior_visit_started_at
columns.description: started_at of this patient's immediately preceding visit in this view; null for a patient's first visit in the 2020-2027 window.

columns.name: days_since_prior_visit
columns.description: Days between this visit and the patient's immediately preceding visit. This is real, patient-specific spacing (some patients visit monthly with gaps, some have single-day visit pairs); it is not a fixed or uniform interval, unlike the synthetic OpenELIS lab dataset. Do not assume it is populated for a patient's first visit.

terminology: Most encounters in this demo instance are typed 'OPD Visit'; two encounter records on the same calendar day for one patient is common (a visit plus a linked form) and does not necessarily indicate two separate clinical visits.

days_since_prior_visit reflects genuine per-patient variation, not a fixed cadence: use it directly to answer visit-frequency or visit-gap questions rather than approximating from encounter counts over a date range.

freshness.updateBehavior: Operator-triggered FULL FHIR_SEARCH against the OpenMRS FHIR2 R4 endpoint; query provenance carries run ID, source watermark, completion state, and observed lag.

examples.question: Show the average number of days between visits for each patient since 2026-01-01.
examples.sql: SELECT patient_id, AVG(days_since_prior_visit) AS avg_days_between_visits, COUNT(*) AS visit_count FROM analytics.hiv_visit_fact_v1 WHERE started_at >= :start_at AND days_since_prior_visit IS NOT NULL GROUP BY patient_id ORDER BY avg_days_between_visits
